items.title: How India’s food prices rose this September
items.summary: In September 2026, a kilogram of onion cost 93% more than last year, while sugar prices were up 28% and rice was up about 8%, on average, according to ISignal’s Food Price Watch dashboard , which uses Department of Consumer Affairs data. This is in a year with the fourth lowest rainfall since the turn of the century, as the country approaches the withdrawal of the monsoon with a 13% deficit. Sustained low prices in past years pushed farmers away from onion, experts say, while the government lists factors such as increased demand and speculation for the increase in sugar prices. “Extreme climate events are raising agricultural risk, disrupting the global food system, increasing the chance of multiple breadbasket failure and pushing up food prices around the world,” a September 2026 analysis by Zero Carbon Analytics noted, adding that “historically unprecedented heat, drought, rain and cold are causing food price spikes across all continents”. It also noted that perishable foods such as fruits and vegetables can face larger price swings because of their limited shelf life and more vulnerable supply chains. ISignal reached out to the Department of Consumer Affairs for comment. We will update this report when we receive a response. Onion farmers cut back after low prices The retail price of onion in September was Rs 52.8, the highest monthly average price since November 2024. Further, since 2014, average monthly prices were higher than this on only eight occasions, our analysis shows. Prices more than doubled since May this year. Last September, retail prices of onion were Rs 27.4, the lowest for that month since 2022. “Onion prices remained low for two to three years. At times, the farmer could not even recover the cost from harvesting the onion, transporting it and taking it to the market, resulting in a negative return,” said Sominath Gholwe, an agricultural researcher. “Because of this, some farmers turned away from onion cultivation.” He explained that it now costs at least Rs 12.5 to produce and bring 1 kg onion to the market, up from around Rs 10. items.title: ECI’s reforms cannot erase past failures
items.summary: Imagine you're a patient in a hospital and the hospital tells you: “From tomorrow, we’ll maintain proper records of every important decision about your treatment. We’ll make sure doctors can make the decisions without being overridden by a computer system. And if something goes wrong, we’ll investigate what happened.” You are not going to say, “Waah - Great reforms.” You would ask: “Hello, Wait. What was happening till yesterday?” That is exactly where we need to begin with the Election Commission of India. After months of questions over its functioning, the ECI has suddenly announced a series of changes: agendas will be circulated, minutes recorded, IT systems screened, and some SIR-affected voters given additional assistance. But these aren't just changes for tomorrow. They raise questions about what happened yesterday: what procedures were followed, who made the decisions, and who authorised them? Let Me Explain. items.summary: 14 मई, 2026 को दिल्ली में एक फिल्म का प्रीमियर हुआ. खुद मुख्यमंत्री रेखा गुप्ता ने फिल्म की स्टारकास्ट के साथ यह फिल्म देखी. अगले दिन 15 मई से यह जनता के लिए सिनेमाघरों में प्रदर्शित हुई. इससे पहले फिल्म का लंबा चौड़ा प्रमोशन हुआ. लेकिन इन सबके बावजूद फिल्म को बॉक्स ऑफिस पर अपेक्षाकृत सफलता नहीं मिली. हम बात कर रहे हैं. संजय दत्त स्टारर ‘आखिरी सवाल’ की. फिल्म का निर्माण निखिल नंदा और संजय दत्त ने निखिल नंदा मोशन पिक्चर्स और नीम ट्री एंटरटेनमेंट के बैनर तले किया है. इसके निर्देशक अभिजीत मोहन वारंग हैं, जिनकी पिछली फिल्म 'पिकासो' को 67वें राष्ट्रीय फिल्म पुरस्कारों में ‘विशेष उल्लेख’ मिला था. फिल्म की कहानी, पटकथा और संवाद उत्कर्ष नैथानी के हैं, संगीत मोंटी शर्मा का है और गीत कुमार विश्वास ने लिखे हैं. संजय दत्त के अलावा फिल्म में नमाशी चक्रवर्ती, अमित साध, समीरा रेड्डी, नीतू चंद्रा, त्रिधा चौधरी, मृणाल कुलकर्णी, निखिल नंदा, अर्चना अय्यर और बिपिन नाडकर्णी हैं. फिल्म की कहानी एक युवा शोधार्थी विक्की हेगड़े (नमाशी चक्रवर्ती) और उसके प्रोफेसर गोपाल नाडकर्णी (संजय दत्त) के बीच बहस की है. यह बहस आरएसएस से जुड़े पांच विवादित सवालों पर होती है, जिनमें गांधी की हत्या में उसकी कथित भूमिका, बाबरी मस्जिद विध्वंस और आपातकाल आदि शामिल हैं. फिल्म के प्रमोशन के दौरान पोस्टर्स पर भी यही पांच सवाल थे. खबरों के मुताबिक फिल्म ने सिनेमाघरों में मात्र 2.45 करोड़ रुपये कमाए. बॉलीवुड हंगामा के बॉक्स-ऑफिस आंकड़े इसे ‘फ्लॉप फिल्म’ की श्रेणी में रखते हैं. बताया जाता है कि इसे बनाने में करीब 30 करोड़ रुपये लगे थे. सामान्य तौर पर यह ऐसा घाटा है जिसकी भरपाई मुश्किल है. लेकिन प्रसार भारती ने शायद इसे इस नज़र से नहीं देखा. दरअसल, सार्वजनिक प्रसारक प्रसार भारती के ‘कंटेंट सोर्सिंग डिवीज़न’ के दस्तावेज़ों पर गई हमारी नजर बताती है कि जून, 2026 तक प्रसार भारती इस फिल्म पर 4.28 करोड़ रुपये खर्च कर चुका है, और मार्च, 2027 तक 4.65 करोड़ रुपये और खर्च करेगा. इस तरह इस फिल्म पर कुल खर्च 8.93 करोड़ रुपये प्रसार भारती खर्च कर रहा है. वहीं, फिल्म में प्रसार भारती का नाम सह-निर्माता के रूप में दिखता है. लेकिन प्रसार भारती इस फिल्म से कब जुड़ा? ये पैसे उसने फिल्म निर्माण के लिए दिए हैं या फिर उसके प्रसारण के लिए? इस बारे में अभी तक प्रसार भारती ने कोई स्पष्ट जानकारी नहीं दी है. आंकड़े खुद कुछ नहीं बताते ये दस्तावेज़ अगस्त में प्रसार भारती के वित्त विभाग के कहने पर जमा किए गए थे. जिसमें खर्च और कमाई का ब्योरा है. न्यूज़लॉन्ड्री को पता चला है कि इनका मकसद प्रसार भारती को वित्त वर्ष की आय का अनुमान पक्का करने में मदद देना था. दस्तावेजों के मुताबिक ‘कंटेंट सोर्सिंग डिवीज़न’ का 2026-27 का कुल बजट लगभग 280 करोड़ रुपये है. इसमें से जून तक 55.96 करोड़ रुपये खर्च हो चुके थे और मार्च 2027 तक करीब 223 करोड़ रुपये और

items.title: Rs 9 crore for Sanjay Dutt-starrer on RSS: The state broadcaster’s favourite box-office flop
items.summary: There is a neat trick some films manage that ordinary films can't: lose money in cinemas and still come out ahead in a government ledger. Aakhri Sawal , starring Sanjay Dutt, has pulled it off. Released on May 15, 2026, after a promotional campaign built around the RSS’s role in some of modern India’s most contested episodes, the film reportedly earned Rs 2.45 crore in its theatrical run – a number Bollywood Hungama ’s box-office data files under “ flop ”. It reportedly cost around Rs 30 crore to make. By conventional arithmetic, that’s a loss hard to recover from. Except Prasar Bharati doesn’t appear to have read it that way. Copies of documents from the public broadcaster’s Content Sourcing Division, reviewed by Newslaundry , show it had spent Rs 4.28 crore on the film by June 2026, with another Rs 4.65 crore projected by March 2027 – a total outlay of Rs 8.93 crore. Prasar Bharati’s name appears in the film’s credit roll as a co-producer. What did the money buy? Was it a stake in the film and its royalties or just a licence to stream it? Or was it something in between? This is what Prasar Bharati is yet to specify. The numbers don’t explain themselves The documents were submitted in August after a request from the broadcaster’s finance department. They cover expenses and earnings, and were meant to help Prasar Bharati confirm its revenue outlook for the financial year, Newslaundry has learnt. The figure is substantial. The Content Sourcing Division’s total budget for 2026–27 stands at nearly Rs 280 crore, of which Rs 55.96 crore had been spent by June and roughly Rs 223 crore more is projected until March 2027. One film accounts for nearly three percent of everything the division will spend across a full year. For comparison, in the same financial year, Prasar Bharati acquired 59 Hollywood films, combined, for Rs 15 crore – roughly Rs 25 lakh a title. Aakhri Sawal cost much more than that. Though it is worth resisting the reflex to treat “flopped at the box office” as the end of the financial story. Theatrical figures rarely capture the corporate arrangements, licensing deals and OTT payouts that increasingly cushion a film’s real economics. But that cuts both ways: if the film’s producers were always going to recover their money elsewhere, the question of what the public broadcaster’s Rs 8.93 crore was doing in the arrangement becomes sharper. items.title: Rs 48 lakh to 2 ex-judges, ‘doubtful voters’: A press club’s costly wait for an election
items.summary: In July 2024, a district court in Jammu handed two retired judges a clear job: get the Jammu Press Club to hold its overdue election, “by all means”, by September 30. It’s been over two years since, and the elections are nowhere in sight. The two former judges are still in place. And the club is still paying them Rs 1 lakh each a month to oversee its accounts: signing off on 49 member staff salaries, bar bills and daily supplies, either from the committee room, or the accounts office, or from their own homes when a club employee is sent over with paperwork. This seems to be a strange arrangement for a body of nearly 870 journalists: an institution whose members spend their working lives asking public offices why their processes have stalled, unable to run a ballot of its own for two years. The former judges refused to clearly specify the amount they have received so far, but by Newslaundry ’s estimates, the club has committed close to Rs 48 lakh to the two men since July 2024. This amount, some members say, could have gone towards repairs the building has not seen since years. Apart from the district court, the matter has also reached the high court. And at the centre of the dispute are two names known to every reporter in Jammu. Sanjeev Pargal, the club president and bureau chief of the Daily Excelsior , the city’s largest newspaper, wants more than 200 “doubtful voters” struck off the rolls before anyone votes. He also wants the general secretary, Dinesh Manhotra, struck off the membership altogether, claiming he is a government employee, and therefore ineligible in the journalist category. Manhotra, on his part, claims the screening of voters is a device to keep Pargal in the president’s chair. He alleges the screening process is aimed merely at harassment. Reached for comment, the two men blunt their aggressive courtroom positions. Pargal told us the points in contest were sub-judice and refused to discuss any of them. Manhotra said the club was a “family” and “this is a family matter”. Neither has responded to our written questionnaire. Newslaundry studied district and high court case orders and spoke to the club’s president, general secretary and apex committee to understand the sequence of events that transpired at the club over the last two years. items.title: Filling the empty vessel: How the Supreme Court now attributes mens rea to companies
items.summary: Corporate criminal liability has always sat awkwardly with the basic idea of a guilty mind. A company, in the old line, has "no soul to damn and no body to kick." It can't form intent the way a person does. Still, companies hold enormous economic power and can-do real harm, so legal systems have had to find ways to make them answer for crimes. In India, the Supreme Court settled in Iridium India Telecom Ltd. v. Motorola Inc. , (2011) 1 SCC 74 , that a company can have mens rea . What it never explained was how : through whom, and on what basis. As the Court put it in Sanofi , that question remained "an empty vessel, yet to be filled." On September 7, 2026, the Court finally filled it with a three-stage framework, built after a careful look at English law from Lennard's Carrying through to the reforms that followed Barclays . This is the first time the Supreme Court has set out a complete doctrinal basis for attributing mens rea to a company. It will change how corporate prosecutions are brought, defended and decided. The facts Sanofi India supplied certain Rare Materials Project to BARC from 2011 to 2016. In 2017 the CBI filed a chargesheet against Dr. P. Anand, a Scientific Officer at BARC, and against Sanofi. The charges were under Section 120B read with Section 420 IPC and several provisions of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988. It was the case of the prosecution that, Dr. Anand conspired with Sanofi to buy medicines at inflated rates by labelling items as proprietary, leaving out competing bidders, or refusing to order from the lowest bidder, and BARC allegedly lost INR 3,53,361 as a result. He allegedly took INR 42,750 in illegal gratification, and Sanofi was said to have abetted it. In this regard, no employees of Sanofi were named as an accused. Sanofi approached the Karnataka High Court under Section 482 CrPC seeking the quashing of the proceedings. Its argument was that a company can't be prosecuted for a mens rea offence unless the person who was its "directing mind and will" is identified and charged alongside it. Relying on Iridium India , the High Court refused. "Whether" and "how" The Supreme Court concluded that it would not be able to quash the ruling of the lower courts until it first decided how Indian law assigns men's rea to the corporation. items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday dismissed a batch of petitions seeking action against politicians for hate speech that allegedly led to the North-East Delhi riots of 2020. A Division Bench of Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain also dismissed a batch of petitions seeking an inquiry by a Special Investigation Team (SIT) into alleged police atrocities that took place in Jamia Millia Islamia in 2019 during a march against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA). A detailed copy of the judgement is awaited. Justices Vivek Chaudhary and Manoj Jain The order was passed in a batch of petitions seeking registration of FIRs against politicians for the speeches they delivered during the CAA and the National Register of Citizens (NRC) protests that allegedly instigated the riots in North East Delhi and ultimately led to the death of over 50 people. One of the petitions, filed by Shaik Mujtaba Farooq, sought registration of FIRs against Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) leaders like Anurag Thakur, Kapil Mishra and Parvesh Sahib Singh Verma. items.title: BRS leader Harish Rao accuses Congress of breaking election promises to minorities
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. Former minister and Bharat Rashtra Samithi (BRS) senior leader Harish Rao, on October 4, accused the Congress-led state government of failing to fulfil its election promises to minorities, farmers and poor families. Speaking at a rights programme organised by the Telangana Turaka Kasha Welfare Association in Gajwel, he said Congress had promised to raise the minority budget to Rs 4,000 crore and implement a Minority Declaration. However, he claimed the government was spending only around Rs 1,300 crore. Harish also alleged that support through the Minority Finance Corporation had declined and that its employees, along with Urdu Academy staff, had faced salary delays. He claimed that the BRS government had spent about Rs 1550 crore on overseas scholarships for minority students over 10 years, compared with around Rs 14 crore under Congress in the last three years. Highlighting development in Gajwel, Harish credited former Chief Minister K Chandrasekhar Rao (KCR) with addressing drinking water shortages and developing irrigation through projects including Kondapochamma Sagar and Mallanna Sagar. He alleged that the Congress government was not lifting available Godavari water to Mallanna Sagar despite functioning infrastructure, calling it a “crisis created by the government”. Harish also criticised the government over pending compensation to Mallanna Sagar project-affected families and delays in Kalyana Lakshmi payments. He said the BRS government had provided rehabilitation packages, including 250-square-yard plots and Rs 5.04 lakh for house construction, to displaced families. Harish alleged that nearly two lakh Kalyana Lakshmi applications were pending and demanded their immediate clearance. items.title: CM Satheesan seeks CPI(M) apology for calling Malappuram a ‘den of fundamentalists’
items.summary: A day after former CPI(M) MLA P Nandakumar described Malappuram as a “den of religious fundamentalists and communalists”, Keralam Chief Minister VD Satheesan on October 4, demanded an unconditional apology from the CPI(M), accusing the party of demonising the Muslim-majority district. In a post on X, Satheesan condemned Nandakumar’s remarks and said that they amounted to “communal slurs” against the people of Malappuram. He also criticised former Chief Minister and CPI(M) leader Pinarayi Vijayan for not objecting to the remarks when they were made in his presence. Satheesan said Pinarayi’s silence suggested the remarks had the “tacit endorsement” of the CPI(M). He accused the party of adopting “dog-whistle politics” by disparaging minority communities and alleged that its repeated criticism of Malappuram reflected an anti-minority shift. Satheesan also demanded that Pinarayi and the CPI(M) Central leadership clarify their position on Nandakumar’s remarks. He questioned the party’s claim to be a progressive and secular organisation and warned of strict action against those promoting communalism. Nandakumar made the remarks during his welcome address at an extended CPI(M) district committee meeting in Ponnani, Malappuram, on October 3. The meeting was attended by Pinarayi and other senior party leaders. “We know that there are unique circumstances regarding Malappuram district. Malappuram district is a den of religious fundamentalists and communalists,” Nandakumar had said. He went on to say that the meeting would discuss how the CPI(M) could unite secular forces, build a broad-based popular movement and address organisational weaknesses in the district. Nandakumar represented Ponnani in the Kerala Assembly from May 2021 to May 2026. Meanwhile, CPI(M) state secretary MV Govindan sought to distance the party from Nandakumar’s remarks, saying the party was ideologically opposed to the influence of communal forces on political organisations, including the Indian Union Muslim League (IUML). Former CPI(M) MLA KT Jaleel also sought to play down the controversy, describing Malappuram as a “haven for secular forces”. Congress leader V S Joy, who represents the Thavanur constituency in Malappuram, similarly defended the district, describing it as a place built by secular-minded people. The Muslim Youth League has meanwhile filed a police complaint against Nandakumar, accusing him of attempting to create communal divisions through his remarks.

items.title: Extreme heat is putting pregnant women and newborns at greater risk, global survey finds
items.summary: Extreme heat is already affecting the health of pregnant women and newborns, with nearly three-quarters of maternal healthcare professionals surveyed across five countries reporting an increase in heat-related cases and complications over the past five years, a new survey commissioned by Wellcome has found. Wellcome is a global charitable foundation that supports science and research to address urgent health challenges, including climate change, infectious diseases and mental health A survey conducted last month of 1,000 healthcare professionals in India, Australia, Brazil, the UK and Zimbabwe found that 73% reported an increase in heat-related cases or complications affecting pregnant women, while 76% reported an increase affecting foetal or newborn health. Nearly all respondents said they had personally cared for a pregnant woman (98%) or a baby (99%) whose health they believed had been adversely affected by extreme heat. The findings were released ahead of the UN climate talks and come as extreme heat intensifies globally. According to an AFP analysis of Copernicus Climate Change Service data, 33 countries recorded their hottest July on record this year. Pregnancy risks Pregnant and postpartum women are particularly vulnerable to extreme heat. Previous research has linked heat exposure to preterm birth, low birth weight, stillbirth and maternal complications. For every 1°C rise in heat exposure, the odds of preterm birth increase by around 5%, while exposure to heatwaves has been associated with a 25% higher risk of obstetric complications, according to a 2024 review of epidemiological evidence. The new survey indicates that healthcare workers are already seeing these risks in clinical settings. About 23% of respondents said they had seen pregnancy complications requiring additional monitoring or treatment that they believed were linked to extreme heat exposure. Healthcare professionals also reported seeing low birth weight or restricted growth (34%), dehydration and heat-related illness among newborns (36%), and difficulties with feeding, breathing and temperature regulation (33%). Extreme heat was also found to affect access to maternal healthcare. items.title: Telangana woman dies in US road crash, family seeks help to bring back mortal remains
items.summary: A 31-year-old woman from Telangana died in a road accident in Missouri, US, after a truck allegedly rammed the car she was travelling in. Daram Supriya, from Maripeda mandal in Mahabubabad district, was returning home after closing her restaurant in St Louis when the accident occurred, her family members told media. According to reports , the accident reportedly took place around 2.20 am on October 5. Supriya died on the spot, while her friend, another woman from Telangana who was travelling with her, sustained serious injuries and was shifted to a hospital for treatment. According to Supriya’s family, the two women were returning home in a car when a truck hit their vehicle from behind. Further details about the circumstances of the accident and the condition of the injured woman are awaited. Supriya had been running a restaurant in St Louis. She had married Kodumuri Ranjith, who works in the software sector, around five years ago. The couple has a two-and-a-half-year-old son. Supriya’s father, Daram Srinivas, has written to Telangana Chief Minister A Revanth Reddy, seeking the state government’s assistance in bringing his daughter’s mortal remains back to India so that the family can perform her last rites. Family members are currently awaiting further information from authorities in the US.
